title: StanceSignal
description: One point of the aggregated social signal S(t) for one market. Published on Redis channel 'augury.signal.<market_id>' by the Python stance pipeline; consumed by augury-engine (C++, drives the LMSR) and augury-api (Java, streams to clients).

ts.description: Timestamp the signal is evaluated at (the 't' in S(t)), not the wall-clock time it was computed.

model_version.description: Stance model identity, e.g. 'vader-3.3.2' or 'deberta-v3-stance-2026.07'. Signals from different model versions are separate series and must not be concatenated.

s_t.description: Weight- and time-decay-weighted mean stance. -1 fully bearish, +1 fully bullish on the market's target proposition.

p_hat.description: s_t mapped into probability space. Required for any Brier comparison against market price, since s_t itself is in [-1,1] and is not a probability.

calibration.description: How p_hat was produced. 'affine' is the assumption-free (s_t+1)/2; 'platt' is a logistic fit on resolved markets. Must accompany p_hat — comparing scores across mappings is meaningless.

n_posts.description: Accepted posts contributing to this point. A small n means a noisy signal regardless of how confident s_t looks.

weight_sum.description: Denominator of the S(t) expression. Near-zero means every contributing post has decayed away and s_t is effectively stale.

half_life_seconds.description: Effective half-life at this point. Varies over time under adaptive decay, so it travels with the signal.
